header: Date: 2026-08-18 09:00 PT | Duration: 51m | Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Reddy (CTO, Meridian), Tom Hale (Lead ML Eng), Aisha Mensah (Platform Eng)
summary: Discovery focused on fast time-to-first-token via self-serve API, pilot sizing for 50k tokens/day, and deciding between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC). Customer has strict compliance needs (SOC2, KMS), wants initial PLG sprint with free credits, and asked for a benchmark with their sample corpus. SE to follow up with security artifacts; AE to send pricing options for pilot and reserved capacity.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment fit
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Khan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account. We got about fifty minutes, want to make sure we cover quickstart, credits, and whether Hosted or Dedicated or a VPC private path makes sense. Liam from SE will cover the technical fit and security.
[00:12] Priya Reddy: Hi Samira, thanks. We just want a clear runway — time to first token, costs for early pilot, and what the private options look like. We're evaluating some other vendors too so understanding tradeoffs is key.
[00:26] Samira Khan: Totally. Quick question on your end: what's your current stack for model orchestration and infra?
[00:31] Tom Hale: We're on GKE for most services, using LangChain-ish adapters, and PostHog for analytics. For ML infra we run a model registry and a tiny inference cluster internally but it's more dev-level; we don't want to manage inference at scale yet.
[00:45] Aisha Mensah: Agree — platform team wants predictable costs and SSO + KMS support. Data residency is a maybe, we have EU-hosted customers.
[00:55] Liam Ortega: Ok, makes sense. For a PLG-first quickstart, the hosted Redwood API is usually the fastest path — sign up, get credits, integrate SDK, first token in minutes. Dedicated is the next step if you need steady throughput and isolation; Private/VPC or on-prem is for strict compliance.
[01:12] Priya Reddy: Can you quantify "minutes"? We have engineers who need to demo features to product by next week.
[01:18] Samira Khan: Realistically, with our self-serve flow and SDK we see TTFT — time to first token — in under an hour for devs who follow the quickstart. If you want a production-like benchmark with your dataset, that takes a week to schedule and run.
[01:30] Tom Hale: The hour figure is helpful. For the pilot we want to exercise a 50k tokens/day workload across a mix of chat and embeddings. Any gotchas for streaming vs batch?
[01:45] Liam Ortega: Streaming is supported in Hosted and Dedicated; embeddings are straightforward. For 50k/day, hosted will be simplest cost-wise; dedicated reserved capacity becomes appealing if sustained traffic and lower unit cost are critical. Also we have automatic batching and KV cache that reduce token costs for chat workloads.
[02:05] Priya Reddy: Security — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), and KMS for key control. Do you support customer-managed keys in private deployments?
[02:15] Liam Ortega: Yes, in our Private (VPC) deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. Hosted supports encryption at rest and TLS, and we offer bring-your-own-key for Dedicated with a managed KMS approach — but customer-managed key in a VPC is the highest-control option.
[02:30] Aisha Mensah: For the initial sprint we prefer Hosted if we can guarantee audit logs and SSO.
[02:36] Samira Khan: Hosted can do SSO via SAML and provides audit logs; we'll share the SOC2 and compliance pack. It comes down to whether you need network isolation or on-prem.
[02:48] Tom Hale: On network isolation, our legal team is sensitive about sending PII-ish transcripts to a hosted vendor. We can scrub or pseudonymize before sending, but want the option to move to VPC later.
[02:59] Liam Ortega: That migration path is supported — same API and SDK across Hosted, Dedicated, Private. You can start on Hosted and slice over to Dedicated or VPC later without rewriting client code. We also provide exportable audit logs to help with compliance.
[03:14] Priya Reddy: Pricing — what's the best way to estimate cost for the 50k tokens/day sample?
[03:21] Samira Khan: We'll model it two ways: hosted PAYG using per-token pricing (we'll send an example calc), and a reserved Dedicated option with a monthly commit that lowers unit cost. For a short pilot (2–4 weeks) free credits cover initial usage; then we can discuss reserved sizing if you want stable capacity.
[03:37] Tom Hale: Free credits — what's typical? We have a small budget for initial experiments.
[03:41] Samira Khan: For PLG quickstarts we typically provision 500–2,000 USD worth of credits depending on the scope — for your pilot we'll provision 1,000 USD (equivalent tokens) which should cover the 50k/day for a week of intense testing.
[03:55] Aisha Mensah: Will those credits let us run a benchmark with our sample corpus?
[03:59] Samira Khan: Yes. We can also coordinate with Liam to run a server-side benchmark for stricter comparatives.
[04:06] Liam Ortega: If you share a small eval set and a couple of representative request traces, we can run a controlled benchmark on Dedicated equivalent infra to show latency and cost profiles. That takes about 3–5 days to schedule and run.
[04:20] Priya Reddy: Good. On the topic of latency, our product needs sub-400ms median for short chat prompts. Can Redwood hit that on Hosted?
[04:30] Liam Ortega: Depends on model selection and sequence length. On Hosted with our low-latency variants we can often get <400ms median for concise prompts, but peak concurrency and cold-starts can affect it. Dedicated with pinned capacity provides more consistent tail latencies.
[04:44] Tom Hale: What about quantized models — we run smaller LLMs in production; how mature is your quantization and kernel optimizations?
[04:52] Liam Ortega: Our runtime supports quantized variants and dynamic kernel selection; we do a lot of inference optimization for common architectures. For your workload we'd recommend a medium-sized quantized variant during pilot to balance latency and quality.
[05:06] Priya Reddy: Any limits on file sizes for embeddings or rate limits when on Hosted?
[05:11] Samira Khan: We have default rate limits on free-tier accounts but those are raised for pilot customers. Embedding size limits depend on model and sequence length; we'll share a short doc with specifics.
[05:22] Aisha Mensah: Compliance checklist — can you email over SOC2, pen test summary, and if you have any ISO docs?
[05:29] Liam Ortega: Yes — we'll attach SOC2 type II, recent pen test summary, and our private deployment checklist. Note some vendor names in those docs might be older, transcription says redwood decayed in one spot, but docs are current.
[05:46] Priya Reddy: (laughs) Noted.
[05:50] Tom Hale: Integration — we use a small microservice that will call the Redwood API. Any SDK language support? We prefer Go and Python.
[05:59] Samira Khan: We have first-class SDKs for Python, Node, and an official Go client in beta. The REST API is straightforward if you want to use your own HTTP client.
[06:08] Tom Hale: Beta Go client is fine. For telemetry we'd like per-route token cost breakdowns to show to finance.
[06:15] Liam Ortega: The Console exposes token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and per-model latency breakdowns; we can also hook in tracing to your existing APM.
[06:24] Priya Reddy: Who needs to be included in follow-ups? I'll loop in legal for the SOC2 review, and product for the benchmark.
[06:31] Aisha Mensah: Platform team should own VPC peering details.
[06:35] Samira Khan: Great. We'll do a short summary and next steps email. We'll provision the credits and send the pilot pricing options. Liam will send security docs.
[06:45] Priya Reddy: What's the expected turnaround on scheduling the benchmark?
[06:48] Liam Ortega: If you send the sample data and traces this week, we can schedule a run for next Wednesday (2026-08-25) and have results within 72 hours after the run.
[06:59] Tom Hale: Ok I'll upload two request traces and a 2k-example corpus by Friday.
[07:04] Samira Khan: Perfect. A few more quick clarifying questions on deployment drift and rollouts — do you need canary rollouts / A/B tests across model versions?
[07:12] Priya Reddy: Yes, product wants a canary policy and automatic fallback in case a newer model regresses.
[07:18] Liam Ortega: Our console supports rollouts — canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a pinned model variant if quality degrades. Quality monitoring hooks can be tied to your eval sets and trigger alerts.
[07:29] Tom Hale: Nice. Also curious about data retention and logs — how long do you keep prompt/response logs by default?
[07:36] Samira Khan: Default retention is 30 days for Hosted telemetry, configurable for Dedicated and Private. For audits we can export logs into your storage or set longer retention as an add-on.
[07:46] Aisha Mensah: And encryption in transit and at rest?
[07:50] Liam Ortega: TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest; in Private we can integrate your HSM/KMS.
[07:57] Priya Reddy: Any known gotchas moving from Hosted to Dedicated or VPC?
[08:02] Liam Ortega: Mostly around networking (peering, IP allowlists) and key management. We plan migrations with a cutover window; user traffic remains compatible because API and SDK don't change.
[08:12] Tom Hale: If we wanted to simulate production load, can you provide a dedicated trial cluster for benchmarking?
[08:18] Samira Khan: We can spin up a Dedicated-equivalent benchmark cluster for the run, yes — that's part of the coordinated benchmark Liam mentioned.
[08:26] Priya Reddy: For cost modeling, can you show us an example monthly commit for a modest reserved pool?
[08:31] Samira Khan: Yes — I'll include a couple of options in the pricing deck: small (single-GPU pool) and medium (multi-GPU) reserved sizes with estimated unit costs.
[08:41] Tom Hale: Great. Any initial timeline constraints on your side for onboarding?
[08:47] Liam Ortega: No hard constraints; pilot can begin immediately once credits are provisioned and the sample data is shared.
[08:54] Samira Khan: Ok, last section: blockers. Anything legal-wise that would stop you from starting a Hosted pilot?
[08:59] Priya Reddy: Legal will want to review SOC2 and the ability to pseudonymize data. If that looks good, no blockers.
[09:06] Aisha Mensah: Platform needs to confirm VPC peering sandbox details.
[09:10] Samira Khan: Understood. We'll follow up with the artifacts and confirm the benchmark schedule.
[09:15] Priya Reddy: Thanks — this was useful.
[09:17] Samira Khan: Thanks everyone, we'll email recap and next steps.
[09:21] [call ends]

What credits will be provisioned for pilot?
Is customer-managed KMS supported for private deployments?

Customer emphasized time-to-first-token and a benchmark with their corpus. AE committed to 1000 USD in credits and a pricing deck; SE to send SOC2 and checklist.
